evals.expected_output: Defaults the scope question toward 'this project', resolves seeds via research_notes_search plus upsert_pointer lookups (no metadata argument), then runs betweenness_centrality or pagerank over that seed set and presents results by node label.
expectations: Asks the Step 1 scope question, offering 'this project' as the recommended default
Resolves seeds via research_notes_search(tags_all=[project_tag]) followed by upsert_pointer per item, not by trying to pass every node in the corpus
Calls upsert_pointer with no metadata argument during seed resolution
Presents results using concept labels or ref_type:ref_id, not bare node ids

evals.prompt: Find a path between attention mechanisms and retrieval-augmented generation.
evals.expected_output: Resolves both concept names to node ids via find_concepts, then calls research_graph_analyze op=paths with from_id/to_id/max_depth, presenting each returned path as a labeled hop sequence.
expectations: Calls find_concepts for both concept names before running the paths op
Uses op=paths with from_id and to_id, not betweenness_centrality or another algorithm
Asks or defaults max_depth reasonably rather than omitting it (max_depth is required for paths)
Presents every returned path, not just the first, since paths returns multiple simple paths by design

evals.expected_output: Flags the whole-graph scope as expensive/rare, asks whether the user wants a raw export or a rendered visualization, then runs graph_export.py export or visualize accordingly rather than attempting a seed-bounded analyze call over every node.
expectations: Explicitly notes that whole-graph scope covers everything ever fetched or noted, not just the current project
Does not attempt to pass every node id into research_graph_analyze as a workaround
Calls shared/scripts/graph_export.py via Bash rather than reimplementing export/visualization logic inline
Asks whether the user wants a raw export (cypher_json/graphml) or a PNG visualization if not already specified
